description: Material-dependent educational screening bands based on when the ideal elastic Euler stress reaches the material yield limit and on the classical Johnson/Euler curve transition. This is not a universal or code design classification.

short_boundary.derivation: Set Euler critical stress sigma_E = pi^2 * E / lambda^2 equal to sigma_y.

intermediate_upper_boundary.derivation: Classical Johnson/Euler transition where Euler critical stress equals one half of yield stress.

assumptions: A positive, verified Young's modulus and yield stress for the selected material condition are available.
For this theoretical screening classification only, the selected material yield stress is assumed to represent the compressive yield limit of an isotropic ductile material.
The yield stress is not treated as a measured compressive/crushing strength and is not used to calculate squash capacity.
The member is straight, prismatic, initially ideal, concentrically loaded, and represented by the entered effective length and least radius of gyration.
These bands are an educational interpretation of classical elastic-yield behavior, not a universal classification standard, code check, or substitute for material- and design-specific verification.
reference: MechanicalC, Column Buckling — Short Compression Members, Slenderness Ratio, Johnson Formula, and Euler/Johnson transition; see also Gere, Mechanics of Materials, column buckling chapter.
